sections.title: Career stages
sections.content:
Vocabulary for describing professional growth and career milestones:
• intern — a trainee gaining work experience. She started as an intern and worked her way up.
• apprentice — someone learning a trade from a skilled employer. He served a three-year apprentice in carpentry.
• promotion — advancement to a higher position. Hard work earned her a well-deserved promotion.
• tenure — the period of holding a position. During his tenure as CEO, profits doubled.
• retirement — leaving work permanently, usually due to age. She's looking forward to a peaceful retirement.

sections.title: Workplace dynamics
sections.content:
Words that describe how workplaces function:
• delegate — assign tasks to others. Good managers know how to delegate effectively.
• collaborate — work together on a project. The two departments collaborated on the product launch.
• micromanage — control every small detail of others' work. Nobody likes being micromanaged by their boss.
• networking — building professional relationships. Attending conferences is great for networking.
• multitask — handle several tasks simultaneously. In this role, you need to multitask constantly.

sections.title: Job challenges
sections.content:
Describing difficulties in professional life:
• burnout — exhaustion from overwork. Working 80-hour weeks led to complete burnout.
• redundancy — losing a job because it's no longer needed. The factory closure resulted in 200 redundancies.
• glass ceiling — invisible barrier to advancement. Many women still face a glass ceiling in corporate life.
• dead-end job — a position with no prospect of progress. He quit his dead-end job to start his own business.

exercises.question: Extreme exhaustion caused by prolonged overwork is called:
exercises.hint: It happens when you work too hard for too long.
exercises.explanation: Burnout is physical or mental collapse caused by overwork or stress.

exercises.question: When a manager controls every small detail of employees' work, they:
exercises.explanation: Micromanage means to control every part of a situation, especially work, in a way that is not wanted.

exercises.question: An invisible barrier preventing career advancement is called a:
exercises.hint: You can't see it but it stops progress.
exercises.explanation: The glass ceiling is an unacknowledged barrier to advancement, especially for women and minorities.

exercises.question: Assigning your tasks to other team members is to:
exercises.explanation: Delegate means to entrust tasks or responsibilities to another person.

exercises.question: Losing your job because the position is no longer needed is:
exercises.hint: The company no longer requires your role.
exercises.explanation: Redundancy is when an employer dismisses workers because their jobs are no longer necessary.

exercises.question: Building professional contacts at events is called:
exercises.explanation: Networking is the action of interacting with others to exchange information and develop professional contacts.

exercises.question: The period during which someone holds a position is their:
exercises.hint: How long they've been in the role.
exercises.explanation: Tenure is the holding of an office or the period for which it is held.

exercises.question: A job that offers no opportunities for advancement is a:
exercises.explanation: A dead-end job is a position with no prospects for promotion or development.
